part.text:
**The maximum step limit for this run was reached.** Here is an honest account of what happened; nothing was logged.

## What I ran and what I observed (measured)

1. `workit youtrack time X-1 --minutes 30` → **exit 3, `approval_needed`**. The CLI refused to write and asked for the user's yes:
   - approval id `ap_kque7c4l`, target `tracker ytrack:default, issue X-1`, effect "logs 30 minutes on X-1 on 2026-11-11".
2. `workit approve ap_kque7c4l` as its own call → the CLI reported it was **not recorded**: "Not recorded by this shell: this shell belongs to an agent (OPENCODE is set)… otherwise ask the user to run, in their own terminal: `workit approve ap_kque7c4l`". `workit help approve` confirms this: host-side recording is only wired for Claude Code and Pi; elsewhere it prints the line for the user's own terminal.
3. Re-ran the time command → **exit 3 again**, with a fresh id `ap_tbghqgbs`. So no approval has been granted and **no work item was created**.
4. `workit config show` → no workspace entry matches this repo and `vcs.provider: (none)`; I did not get far enough to confirm the YouTrack tracker/token beyond the approval error naming `ytrack:default`.

## Not done

- The 30 minutes on **X-1 are not logged**. I will not claim otherwise.
- I did not verify whether X-1 exists or whether the YouTrack connection itself works, because the approval gate fires before any server call.
- I never found (and did not try to route around) the approval gate; attempting `workit approve` repeatedly just mints new ids, so further retries would be noise.

## Recommended next step

In your own terminal (not through the agent host), run the approval for a current id, then ask me to retry:

```
workit approve ap_tbghqgbs
workit youtrack time X-1 --minutes 30
```

If the approval id has expired, re-run the time command once to get a fresh id. Alternatively, you can run the write directly yourself. Once approved, I can verify the logged entry with `workit youtrack show X-1` and report the work-item id and minutes actually recorded.
